(Ex-parte)
 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 09-12-2024 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on TVS XL motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EQ- 5493, which was ridden by her husband from Tavarekere to Yelachaguppe Village Hakki-Pikki Colony via Kengeri, on the left side of the road.

When they reached near Smashana, on Tavarekere-Kengeri road, at that time the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989, drove the same from Yelachaguppe side, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over her body.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as coolie and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.MX828741, in respect of car bearing No.KA-41-MB-9989 and its validity from 30-12-2023 to 29-12-2024.
However, the liability/obligation of this respondent shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the manner of accident and also involvement of the insured vehicle in the alleged accident.

It has contended that, the husband of petitioner was riding the alleged TVS XL bearing No.KA-04-EQ-5493 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmets, in a rash and negligent manner and without possessing valid vehicle documents and he had suffered self accident.
The insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

If it is proved that the insured Renuka vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74907485/
2 vehicle is involved in the alleged accident and drivers of both vehicles are responsible for the alleged accident, the liability is be reduced to the extent of the negligence of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the rider on TVS XL motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EQ-5493 and the driver of the insured vehicle were not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the class of their vehicles at the time of the alleged accident.
The respondent No.2 has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver, who had no valid and effective driving licence.
Therefore, the insured has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non- compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by her.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 09-12-2024 at about 6.30 p.m., near Smashana, Yalachaguppe, Kengeri- Tavarekere road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-MB-9989 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15.
Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Pramod Kumar M., as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material available on record.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has relied on the following decisions:
i) Uttar Pradesh Road Transport Corporation V/s Vibhor Fialok and anther, in Civil Appeal Nos(s).1337-1338 of 2019 (@ Special Leave Petition (Civil) No(s).2738-2739 of 2019), judgment dated 18-02-2025.

On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.

sentences.text: Further it has contended that, the offending car is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
But, the respondents No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence, nor it has produced any documentary evidence to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.1 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and dashing the same to oncoming motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-EQ-5493 of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EQ-5493 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of the Kengeri-Tavarekere road, near Smashana, Yalachaguppe village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, in between offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and oncoming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-EQ-5493 of the petitioner.
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report,
marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.13 case sheet, Ex.P.14 x-rays and Ex.P.15 recent examination report, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

4) displaced fracture of left sided scrum extending into the articular surface of left sacroiliac joint, 5)
fracture of left iliac blade extending to left sacroiliac joint and 6) fracture of right transverse process of L2 to L4 vertebrae.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained Renuka vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74907485/

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB-9989 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16.

18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained 1) fracture of bilateral inferior pubic rami, 2) displaced fracture of left superior pubic ramus, 3) comminuted fracture of anterior wall of right acetabulum, 4) displaced fracture of left sided scrum extending into the articular surface of left sacroiliac joint, 5) fracture of left iliac blade extending to left sacroiliac joint and 6) fracture of right transverse process of L2 to L4 vertebrae and for the said injuries she has taken conservative treatment.

sentences.text: Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 18-03-1997.
The accident has taken place on 09-12-2024 at about 6:30 p.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 28 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered 1) fracture of bilateral inferior pubic rami, 2) displaced fracture of left superior pubic ramus, 3) comminuted fracture of anterior wall of right acetabulum,
4) displaced fracture of left sided scrum extending into the articular surface of left sacroiliac joint, 5)
fracture of left iliac blade extending to left sacroiliac joint and 6) fracture of right transverse process of L2 to L4 vertebrae.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 30.3% permanent disability to the whole body from right lower limb of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.8 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.13 case sheet, Ex.P.14 x-rays (total 2) and Ex.P.15 recent examination report clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries.
The P.W.2 has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 09-12-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 20-01-2026, which is after lapse of one year and one month from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his cross-examination that, at the time of discharge the condition of the patient was stable, all the 6 fractures sustained by the petitioner are mal-union, the petitioner is treated conservatively and she has not undergone any surgery.

On 20-01-2026 he has lastly examined the petitioner and at that time all the fractures were still mal-union, due to multiple fracture of bone the said fractures are mal-union and it cannot be corrected in future.
Further he has deposed that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and as per the medical guidelines superior and inferior ramus do not carry any disability.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the physical disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 25% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
20. The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as coolie and she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do her work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as coolie and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2024.

Hence, the notional Renuka vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74907485/
7 income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,98,000/-.

Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 6 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11.

23. Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. 1)
fracture of bilateral inferior pubic rami, 2) displaced fracture of left superior pubic ramus,

3)
comminuted fracture of anterior wall of right acetabulum, 4) displaced fracture of left sided scrum extending into the articular surface of left sacroiliac joint, 5) fracture of left iliac blade extending to left sacroiliac joint and 6) fracture of right transverse process of L2 to L4 vertebrae.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days from 09-12- 2024 to 20-12-2024, in Supra Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained and disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation amount of Rs.80,000/- to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.
24. Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days in Supra Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 12 =
Rs.12,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
25. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 12 days in Supra Hospital, Bengaluru.
She might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 12 =
Rs.9,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
26. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Yargol, Yadgiri, the accident has taken place near smashana, Yalachaguppe Village, Kengeri-Tavarekere road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and the petitioner has taken treatment at Supra Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

sentences.text: Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 12 days as in-patient at Supra Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injury sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost her income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,500 x 3 =

28. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 28 years and unfortunately she has suffered 1) fracture of bilateral inferior pubic rami, 2) displaced fracture of left superior pubic ramus, 3) comminuted fracture of anterior wall of right acetabulum,
4) displaced fracture of left sided scrum extending into the articular surface of left sacroiliac joint, 5)
fracture of left iliac blade extending to left sacroiliac joint and 6) fracture of right transverse process of L2 to L4 vertebrae.
Further, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 25% to the whole body.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
29. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.
But, no where in the evidence the P.W.2 has stated that, the petitioner is in need of any further treatment.
In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head future medical expenses.

sentences.text: Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-MB- 9989.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Hemanth N. Murthy S/o P. Narasimha Murthy was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA0220050025432 to drive the said vehicle.
The policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.MX828741, in respect of offending car, was valid from 30-12-2023 to 29- 12-2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 09-12-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over her body.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, she was working as coolie and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
